## 3. Module Boundary Diagnosis

### S05 structural decisions

| Responsibility | Decision | Reason / constraint |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Extensions coordination, claim identity and immutable catalogs | Keep current module and approved generated import boundary. | F-001/F-003/F-008 remain justified; fix the specific admission/order/diagnostic seams without a new facade or package split. |
| Historical codec compatibility | Remove from the connected Extensions-to-Recovery contract chain. | Explicit pre-production decision E-037; a mandatory empty list would preserve unnecessary burden. |
| Restore-time validation | Keep generic orchestration and structural validation with Recovery/shared storage owners; keep profile semantic validation at later claim admission. | EXT-REQ-138/235, Table 23-E and NF-REQ-184; F-016. Source contribution ownership remains Extensions. |
| Positive historical capture implementation and test-only construction | Replace positive evidence with current-path tests, then remove obsolete machinery; move pure fixture construction into tests. | F-014/F-017. Preserve minimal retired-format rejection evidence and currently required ledger integrity. |
| Browser, security and operational consumers | Audit their existing owners and exact Extensions boundary. | F-018; no wholesale ownership reassignment or feature redesign is preselected. |
| Recovery schema and generation facts | Resolve required codec roles from authored machine inputs and verify their agreement with actual emitted formats; derive table membership from migrations and the frozen catalog. | E-234; bounded schemas avoid duplicated cardinalities. Current-only admission rejects stale or self-consistent incompatible metadata before restore mutation. |

The following original boundary diagnosis remains useful at its stated scope; it is not a complete readiness verdict.

The target is a **legitimate immutable coordination facade plus mutation coordinators**, with a **persistence-adjacent Recovery contribution**. It is not just a thin pass-through facade: registry admission, dependency closure, state protocol and inactive-job classification hide real decisions. The inspected main-package production imports do not include HTTP/authentication, PostgreSQL/pgx, concrete profile implementations, or test-util. Recovery contribution SQL is a distinct exception to the storage-free main-package posture.

### WS-14 completion checkpoint — logical codecs and bounded proofs

WS-14/T-031 is complete before WS-23 starts. The authored Network Flow logical
row definition contains the exact five families, fields, nullability and identity
tuples reviewed manually against adopted NF-REQ-184/Table 25-A. Five declarative
physical maps are packaged alongside it. Physical binding selectors bind mapping
digests; logical proof bytes exclude physical names. Codec schema projections,
source index and provenance were updated and regenerated through Make.

Extensions resolves the required current definition, exact maps, algorithms and
bounds into immutable typed codecs. The shared `internal/platform/extensioncodec`
package encodes logical values and computes EXT-REQ-235 proofs using bounded
metadata chunks and a confined multi-pass merge. It preserves UTF-8, integers,
microseconds, nulls and tuple order; rejects duplicate identities and overflow;
and removes its private scratch data on success, failure or cancellation. It has
no profile callback or database dependency. Recovery composition now carries the
admitted codec and table mapping directly. The redundant Network Flow physical
table lookup API and its production-surface allowance were removed after consumer
inspection. Catalog copy isolation remains covered.

This closes F-019's projection/resolution/shared-support gap. Actual PostgreSQL
catalog/type admission, consistent snapshot reads, ordered restore/readback proofs
and removal of the remaining semantic restore callback are still required in
WS-10. These pure-code and composition results do not establish current Recovery
round-trip or module readiness. F-028's full integrity/companion admission remains
the next required workstream; it is not inferred from canonical-byte checks.
